index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure presents a conceptual diagram illustrating the components of an optimization problem and their interrelationships. The global layout is hierarchical and flow-oriented, with six main rectangular nodes arranged in a top-down structure, connected by directed arrows labeled with relationship types. At the top center is the 'Elements' node, serving as the root or source component. From this node, two directed edges branch downward: one labeled 'Own' points to 'Data Parameter' on the left, and another labeled 'Link' points to 'Decision Activities' on the right. Both 'Data Parameter' and 'Decision Activities' then feed into a central node labeled 'Calculations', via arrows labeled 'Participate', indicating that both contribute to or are involved in calculations. From 'Calculations', two distinct paths emerge: one arrow labeled 'Define the measure in the objective' points to 'Objective Criterion' at the bottom left, and another labeled 'Define the left-hand side of a constraint' points to 'Specifications' at the bottom right. Additionally, a curved arrow originates from 'Elements' and points to 'Specifications', labeled 'Applied on', suggesting that elements are applied directly to specifications. All nodes are uniformly styled as rounded rectangles with light gray fill, dark gray borders, and bold black text. The arrows are solid black lines with classic arrowheads, and all labels are placed near the arrows in plain black text. The diagram visually represents a workflow where elements define data and decision activities, which together participate in calculations that ultimately define the objective criterion and constraints (specifications), with elements also being directly applied to specifications. This structure reflects a formal modeling approach to optimization problems, emphasizing the derivation of objective functions and constraints from underlying data and decision components.
